subject.title: security fix(agents): close symlink-then-.. workspace boundary bypass in assertSandboxPath

question: Should this path-level POSIX mitigation land now with the non-atomic boundary explicitly retained, while https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/114382 owns atomic containment for final-boundary callers?
rationale: The patch’s scope is technically bounded, but accepting a path validator as defense-in-depth rather than a complete filesystem sandbox is a security-contract decision for the subsystem owner.

options.title: Land as defense-in-depth
options.body: Accept the POSIX validation hardening while keeping the linked atomic fs-safe issue open and ensuring future raw-path callers do not rely on this check as their final boundary.

options.title: Wait for atomic adoption
options.body: Hold this PR until an operation-time beneath-root primitive and the affected caller migrations can land together.

recommendation.title: Land as defense-in-depth
recommendation.body: Accept the POSIX validation hardening while keeping the linked atomic fs-safe issue open and ensuring future raw-path callers do not rely on this check as their final boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch refinements and the linked atomic fs-safe follow-up place this security-boundary decision closest to their current ownership trail.
